video.title: The Most Overlooked Way to Make Money On the Internet

summary: Chris Koerner interviews Freychu, a solo operator who builds SEO-driven niche directory websites. He owns six directories (three fully built) that draw roughly 70-90k organic monthly visitors and earn about $2,300-$3,000/month passively. The episode walks through finding niches via Ahrefs 'near me' keyword research (low keyword difficulty, decent volume), analysing example directories (dry ice, movie locations, towing capacity), tooling, monetisation and a cheap backlink-swap tactic. Key takeaway: directories are slow-burn SEO assets; pick low-competition niches, build ugly-but-useful mobile-friendly sites, enrich the data, and buy a few high-quality swapped backlinks.

speakers.name: Freychu
speakers.description: Directory builder and SEO operator who posts on X and YouTube and runs a free community; owns six directory sites

ideas.name: Niche SEO directory portfolio (thrifting directory and others)
ideas.one_liner: Build location/data directories around under-served search queries, rank organically and monetise passively with display ads and small digital products.
ideas.business_model: Display ads (Mediavine Journey), digital product sales, optionally sponsored listings/affiliate
ideas.customer: Consumers searching for specific local or niche information (thrift stores, dog parks, flea markets, plasma donation, etc.); advertisers as the paying side
ideas.problem: Google Maps and generic results handle very specific location or niche queries poorly, leaving more search demand than good supply
ideas.offer: A specialised directory website with enriched, filterable data answering a narrow query set

pricing.model: Free to users; monetised via ads and a digital product

price_points.label: PDF built in Canva sold on one directory

pricing.notes: RPM about $16-17 on the thrifting niche; Mediavine main network denied for the first directory, accepted into Mediavine Journey

acquisition_channels.details: 100% organic; keyword research in Ahrefs, exact-match-style domains, programmatic pages, and backlinks built by paying sites to swap a competitor's link for his (e.g. $50 swap).

quote.text: That's really my main distribution channel I only deal with organic and I mainly deal with like passive evergreen niches.
quote.speaker: Freychu

ideas.delivery: One person builds the site in WordPress with Elementor Pro, GeoDirectory, WP Import and JetEngine; data is collected and enriched with AI; then the site is left alone. He says he hasn't touched his sites for about six months.
unit_economics_claims: Three profitable directories earn about $2,300-$3,000/month combined passively
Traffic of about 70-90k monthly visitors across the sites
One $50 backlink led to rank 1 and about $2,000-$2,500/month in the thrift niche over two years
ideas.startup_cost: About $100 for a domain and basic hosting per the host; Ahrefs is about $150/month
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Slow: months for SEO to rank; he says it took months to find out his first directory worked

acquisition.how: SEO is inbound; agents can do keyword research, content and data pages. Backlink outreach to sites (mostly companies) can be semi-automated but needs human approval and payment.

onboarding.how: No customers to onboard on the consumer side; ad networks are a one-off setup.

delivery.how: Data collection, enrichment, page generation and updates can be agent-driven with occasional human QA.

billing.how: Ad network and digital product payouts are automatic.

support.how: Minimal support; occasional listing corrections or emails.

uk_applicability.notes: SEO and display ads work the same in the UK. Examples are US-centric and UK volumes are smaller, so niches need UK keyword validation. Mediavine and Ezoic are available. GDPR and cookie consent are needed for ads and for any business data scraped about sole traders.

risks: Google core updates and AI overviews can cut informational traffic
Slow to rank, with uncertain payoff
Copycats can quickly clone a successful niche
Ahrefs traffic data is third-party and can be inaccurate
Low-ceiling income unless sponsored listings are sold

tactics.name: Find directory niches with the 'near me' keyword method
steps: Open Ahrefs Keywords Explorer and search 'near me'
Skip branded keywords (Target, McDonald's)
Scroll deep, sorting by keyword difficulty; look for low KD (green) with decent volume
Aim for KD at or below about 20 generally, 0-5 for beginners; volume of 15k-60k worked best
Reject product-led or fad queries where e-commerce dominates (e.g. Dubai chocolate)
Check search intent and narrow broad terms (e.g. 'emergency towing')

quote.text: I find a lot of promise in keywords that hover around like 15,000 monthly search volume to like 60,000
quote.speaker: Freychu

tactics.name: Use a 'bounty' competitor as validation
steps: Find a mom-and-pop-looking site already getting traffic in the niche
Check its traffic in Ahrefs Site Explorer
Judge whether you can beat it; being 2nd-5th can still pay
Snipe its keywords and backlinks

quote.text: finding a website that already succeeded that looks like kind of a mom and pop publisher
quote.speaker: Freychu

tactics.name: Backlink swap outreach
steps: Pull the competitor's backlinks in Ahrefs
Contact the sites linking to them
Offer about $50 to swap their link to yours (not just add)
Prefer pages with high domain rating, real traffic, and few outbound links
Avoid bulk Fiverr or low-quality link services; if buying, route through an intermediate article

quote.text: Can I pay you 50 bucks to swap out the link for ours
quote.speaker: Freychu

tactics.name: Validate demand with Reddit, TikTok and Google Maps reviews
steps: Search Reddit for the question; many threads signal unmet need
Use TikTok comments for unfiltered social listening
Read Google Maps review tags
Spend a couple of hours reading threads to find nuance for the directory's value

tactics.name: Programmatic build with data enrichment
steps: Collect location data in a database
Bulk import with WP Import and publish with GeoDirectory
Add filters with JetEngine (e.g. fenced area for small dogs)
Use AI to enrich listings with answers visitors need
Make it mobile-friendly; design matters less

tactics.name: Stack low-effort sites and wait
steps: Launch a directory and build another while you wait
Expect months for SEO results
Monetise only after traffic: ads, digital products, affiliate

quote.text: while you wait go build another one and then another one

lessons.lesson: Directories are slow passive SEO assets; expect months before traffic, so run several in parallel rather than judging one after two weeks.

quote.text: People are like I don't see any progress two weeks after I launched my directory
quote.speaker: Freychu

lessons.lesson: Choose passive over maximum revenue: display ads on many sites give lower ceilings but avoid becoming a sales or agency business.

quote.text: at a certain point you become a sales business
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

lessons.lesson: Niche selection beats design: balance low keyword difficulty with search volume, and pick evergreen subjects unlikely to change.
Utility beats polish; mobile-friendliness matters more than modern design since about 80% of visitors are on mobile.
Constraints can drive creativity; treat the first project as a skill-learning playground (SEO) and monetise later.

quote.text: it was more of a playground to learn the skill
quote.speaker: Freychu

lessons.lesson: Cheap targeted link swaps can beat expensive link-building services; one link can transform a site's rankings.
Check monetisation potential before choosing a niche: RPMs vary hugely (gaming low, finance high), so traffic alone doesn't indicate revenue.
Use AI mainly for data enrichment that saves visitors time, not just for ideas; user-generated content gives better ideation signal.
Mine your own life moments (moving, graduation, hobbies) for directory ideas, since your experience gives unique angles.
Sharing the domain publicly invites copycats; keep winning niches quiet.

evidence_quality.rationale: The guest is a first-hand operator with consistent, plausible figures (~$2.3-3k/month, 70-90k visitors) but unverified, with no screenshots of revenue shown. Estimates for third-party sites (movie-locations, Penguin) are guesses from Ahrefs. The guest withholds domains, limiting verification. Tactics are specific and credible.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Freychu runs a free community and sells enrich.directory; the host promotes his own newsletter/podcast (tkopod.com). The host says the guest has nothing to sell, but the enrichment tool is a product.
